WASHINGTON — Dr. Anthony Fauci’s pardon from Joe Biden won’t save him from prosecution for obstructing Congress, Sen. Rand Paul warned on Wednesday.

Fauci, in a shocking move, invoked the Fifth Amendment more than 100 times before the Senate

Paul set a committee vote of Aug. 5 to pass a resolution holding Fauci in contempt of Congress for dodging the questions.

“It’s against the law to obstruct an investigation of Congress. There will be repercussions to your refusal to testify,” Paul said.

Fauci was subpoenaed to appear Wednesday by Paul, who has long sparred with the former White House chief medical adviser over the origins of COVID-19 and the practice of government-funded gain-of-function research, in which pathogens are made more virulent for the purpose of preventing global pandemics.

The COVID outbreak, which began in late 2019 in the city of Wuhan, China, is confirmed to have killed more than 7 million people worldwide while shutting down the global economy and forcing millions of American kids out of schools for a full academic year — stunting learning and social development.

“Let’s just get one thing straight,” Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) warned Fauci when his turn came to grill the 85-year-old doctor. “You don’t have any rights under the Fifth Amendment because you’ve been pardoned, as you very well know, as the Supreme Court has been clear for a century and more. Brown vs. Walker, 1896, ‘When he has been pardoned, he may not stand upon his privilege.'”

“You know that. Your lawyers sitting behind you now, shifting nervously in their chairs, they know it,” Hawley went on. “This isn’t about the Constitution. This isn’t about the law. This is about contempt, contempt for this body and contempt for the American people.”

item.description:

https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/6002107-trump-miller-ceuta-spain-migrant-crisis

President Trump and White House deputy chief of staff for policy Stephen Miller are warning that Spain’s Ceuta migrant crisis could be a reality for Americans if Democrats win in future elections.

Some 60,000 migrants have entered Ceuta, an autonomous city of Spain on the North African coast, Ceutan President Juan Jesús Vivas said, according to The Associated Press. They have come from Morocco over the past 24 hours, and more than 40 have died.

“It’s terrible. Remember that picture. That’s going to be us in three years if the wrong side gets in,” Trump told Fox News’s Jacqui Heinrich on Friday. “If the Democrats get in, you will not live a very good life.”

Miller, in a social media post reposting a video of the migrants breaching Spain’s border, said, “Democrats did this to America every single day for 4 years under Biden.”

He said, they “will do it again instantaneously, but orders of magnitude greater, if they are given any form of national power.”

“Democrats will see your home trampled and stolen by invaders and they will rejoice,” Miller wrote.

Spain Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez traveled Friday to Ceuta and condemned the action. He blamed human smugglers, the AP reported, saying they “deceive so many young people, and ultimately lead many of them to their deaths — whether in the ocean or, as in this case, at Spain’s border in the autonomous city of Ceuta.”

Immigration was a significant topic for Republicans in the 2024 election cycle, with Trump vowing to ramp up immigration enforcement. He has since deported hundreds of thousands of illegal immigrants and sent federal troops to several U.S. cities to crack down on illegal immigration.

Republicans are hoping to carry that momentum into the midterms.

item.title: [ 89] Poll: Trump’s MAGA voters would stick by a candidate through the most serious of scandals
item.description:
https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/30/maga-trump-scandal-2026-elections-01013859

Americans are largely tolerant of scandals among politicians. But nobody is more willing to stick by an embattled candidate than a MAGA voter.

The POLITICO Poll finds President Donald Trump’s MAGA supporters are the most loyal of any group of voters — with majorities saying they would stick by GOP candidates confronted with an array of scandals, from a DUI conviction or accepting lobbyist gifts to more serious accusations including domestic violence, sexual assault and antisemitic social media posts.

Two-thirds of self-identified MAGA Trump voters say they would continue supporting a GOP candidate accused of sexual assault — 13 percentage points higher than the share of Trump 2024 voters writ large, which include those who do not identify as MAGA. By comparison, 40 percent of voters who backed former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024 would continue backing a Democratic candidate accused of sexual assault.

item.title: [ 33] Republicans start pondering another debt limit hike as midterms loom
item.description:
https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/07/29/congress/debt-limit-reconciliation-01015197

Republicans raised the debt limit by $5 trillion last year. Now they are already thinking about how to head off another dive over the fiscal cliff on President Donald Trump’s watch.

Independent forecasters predict the U.S. will reach the “X-date” — the ultimate deadline for preventing a U.S. debt default — sometime between next summer and early 2028, just as presidential primaries start kicking into gear.

To head off high-stakes negotiations with Democrats, White House officials have privately floated raising the nation’s $41.1 trillion borrowing limit in the party-line spending package many Republicans want to enact before the November midterm elections, according to two people granted anonymity to disclose private conversations.

The move could save Trump much angst if Republicans lose control of either chamber in the upcoming election, since any Democratic majority would demand concessions in a bipartisan negotiation to prevent an unprecedented default on the national debt, which currently sits at nearly $39.7 trillion.

item.title: [ 50] Apocalypse arrives in Spain
item.description:
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jul/30/thousands-enter-spanish-enclave-ceuta-morocco-africa

The Spanish government is deploying extra troops and police officers to its north African enclave of Ceuta after thousands of people swam and waded into the tiny territory from neighbouring Morocco in a matter of hours.

Videos shot at Tarajal beach on Thursday showed crowds of people walking around the breakwaters and running on the beach and roads.

Most appeared to be young men, but there were also families with women and children. “Viva España!” some shouted to a freelance photographer working for the Associated Press, who was filming the scene.
Hundreds of migrants run and cheer as they enter Spain’s enclave of Ceuta

A spokesperson for the Guardia Civil force, which polices Spain’s borders, said the migrants were “massively entering from the sea” through the Tarajal breakwater but could not provide an estimate of the numbers.

Spain’s national broadcaster, TVE, reported that between 2,000 and 3,000 people had crossed into Ceuta, while the state news agency, Efe, said some had entered the territory by scaling the high border fence.

“The situation is absolute chaos,” said Rachid Sbihi, the head of the association that represents Guardia Civil officers in Ceuta. “It’s not possible to give precise numbers, but there are thousands of migrants crossing.” He added that the border had “totally collapsed”.

Agence France-Presse quoted a government spokesperson as saying that nine bodies had been recovered.

Achraf Maimouni, a member of the Moroccan Association for Human Rights, described the situation as “exceptional”. He said the Tarajal border had been opened “under unusual circumstances” on Thursday morning and people had crossed over.

During a Feb. 1, 2020, phone call with leading scientists, some officials felt certain the virus “could occur naturally,” while others “felt that deliberate insertion” was possible. The two leading scientific theories are that the virus officially known as SARS-CoV-2 jumped from animals to humans at a wet market in Wuhan, China, or it leaked from the Wuhan Institute of Virology, where researchers study coronaviruses.

item.title: [ 41] GOST Communist food.
item.description:
Boomers often say that food was better in the Soviet Union because of GOST, basically the Government standardized everything to a way higher level than what you get today which was kept extremely strict until Gorbachev era, which means the general quality of things was way higher, especially snack foods, soft drinks etc.
So the question is, for those who grew up in Soviet/Post-Soviet Countries, and had access to actual GOST foods, what were the best foods that saw a noticable drop in quality post Gorbachev/Post-Soviet era? I hear ice cream is one of the notable ones, along with Doctors Sausage.
For example Doctor's Sausage GOST:
>Meat
>250 g high-quality lean beef (top grade, trimmed of sinew)
>700 g semi-fat pork (shoulder works well; around 25–30% fat)
>30 g egg (about ½–1 egg, beaten)
>20 g whole milk powder (or a small amount of fresh milk, adjusted for texture)
>Seasoning
>20–21 g salt
>2 g sugar
>0.05 g nutmeg or cardamom (a tiny pinch)
>~0.07 g sodium nitrite (scaled from the original; use a properly measured curing salt instead of raw nitrite)
>The original formula was approximately:
>25% beef
>70% pork
>3% egg
>2% milk
>salt, sugar, nitrite, and nutmeg/cardamom
Compared to Post-GOST the recipe became
>350 g mechanically separated chicken or pork trim
>250 g pork fat/back fat
>150 g pork mince
>150 g ice water
>Fillers & binders
>80 g potato starch
>30 g soy protein isolate or textured soy protein (hydrated)
>20 g skimmed milk powder
>5 g wheat fibre (optional)
>Seasoning
>18 g salt
>3 g sugar/dextrose
>2 g monosodium glutamate (MSG)
>1 g white pepper
>0.3 g nutmeg

/rcg/ was initially created as a way for the roller coaster enthusiasts on here to discuss all things roller coasters and theme parks. item.title: [114] /twg/ - Taiwan General
item.description:
> why no Taiwan general in the catalog edition, grok writing the OP edition

Quick Start Guide for First Timers:

Visa: Most countries get 90 days visa-free. Check if you need an eVisa or ARC if staying longer. Fill out your arrival card online before arriving for less stress.
Best Time: Oct–Dec for perfect weather (dry season). Avoid July–Sept typhoon season unless you like rain and chaos.
Getting Around: Taipei MRT is clean, cheap, and efficient as fuck. Youbike only needs an easy card and is essentially free unless you want to ride for hours.
High Speed Rail (HSR) for city hopping (Taipei Kaohsiung in ~1.5h).
Scooters are god outside Taipei. Get an international permit if you plan to ride.
Uber works but taxis are cheap. Avoid during rush hour or rain.

Food:

Night markets are mandatory. Shilin, Raohe, Ningxia, etc.
Must eats: Beef noodle soup, stinky tofu (acquired taste), oyster omelettes, bubble tea (original homeland), pineapple cake, mango shaved ice. All you can eat hotpot also.
7-11 and FamilyMart are better than in most countries, you can live off them if you want.

Top Spots:

Taipei: 101, Jiufen old street, Beitou hot springs, temples everywhere.
Taroko Gorge (east coast) — absolute kino nature.
Sun Moon Lake, Kenting (beaches), Alishan for mountains.
East coast for chill vibes and fewer tourists.

General Tips:

Taiwanese people are polite and helpful. Learn basic Mandarin or use Google Translate.
Tipping is not expected.

Useful Links & Services:

Official Taiwan Tourism: https://eng.taiwan.net.tw/
YouBike: https://en.youbike.com.tw/
EasyCard: Buy at MRT/7-11 — https://www.easycard.com.tw/en/
HSR: https://www.thsrc.com.tw/
Hot Springs: https://taiwanhotspring.net/ + https://eng.taiwan.net.tw/m1.aspx?sNo=0002035

item.title: [ 63] slug/snailmons thread
item.description:
Those fun facts you see online about how Slugma is so hot it would blind you and singe everything within a country mile are all very wrong, I'm sorry. People who say this don't actually know how thermodynamics works. Yes it's as hot as the surface of the sun, but that's not as big a deal as it sounds. In reality;

>Slugma would glow in the dark, but not be blinding. just a tad brighter than real lava
>Slugma would not melt through the floor (unless it was a really shit floor or it stayed in one spot for hours)
>Slugma would be mildly uncomfortable to stand right next to, but you could stand ~5 feet away without worry of any danger

Vsauce lied to you. (also pls give them a fire/steel 3rd stage evo in gen x based on those geothermal vent snails with metal shells, I'm begging you)

item.title: [266] >begin digital nomad >hear thailand is great for exercise, healthy foods, chea
item.description:
>begin digital nomad
>hear thailand is great for exercise, healthy foods, cheap living, good bars, paradise for this kind of stuff
reality:
>Beers are overpriced in all pubs 3.5-4 USD for CHANG piss, want to drink from 711? LOL nope not till 11AM not even Muslim Malaysia is this bad, so if you work US timezone you better remember to fully stock
>Bars either filled with old Europoors or ~finding myself~ mid-20-somethings who shit up the atmosphere 1/2 a second after bringing up I am American
>Food is kinda not that healthy? Everything is fried and questionable. Decent meals are 7-12 dollars if eating out. "cooking at your place" is cheap but it was in the US
>Living cheap is okay I guess, sure 475/mo for a half way decent studio is fine I guess. Cheap places want some stupid amount for electricity and utilities.
>Internet seems shit, it's either fine until rain or weird latency issues especially during storms. Very weird how little free wifi is at places you think would have it.
>Gyms here suck, tried to come here to get shredded but the lack of hygiene by locals and the annoying old timers that just hang out to hit on the girls on the treadmills is weird also why does every song here have to be some shitty cover of a good American song?
>Tourist spots all look way better in the picture
>air quality keeps making me get Claritin but for some retarded reason can only buy in packs of 10
>beach is okay I guess? I'd rather just zip down to PR though.
>DUDE WEED LMAO everywhere is really fucking annoying from the streets to the beach. Fuck I thought I was in LA's bullshit again.

I don't really see the value savings wow 4 dollars for Chinese budlight amazing or 300B for chicken and rice with egg. People made it sound like flaunting a few bucks here and there made your weekend that of a king, as if. I think I spent less in Seoul all things considered while having a higher standard of living, here I couldn't be more unimpressed. Why does this shit get so much praise?
